request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about how the product moves or what it fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when one of these declarations has the harness measure it; "how" names it: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, a hinge that opens to 110°, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while a part moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off the assembled product), screw (a thread printed on the parts, such as a jar and its cap; not a bought screw or bolt), drives (gears or a rack that turn each other), print_in_place (a product printed already assembled), standard (the fit of one of these four bought parts, and no other: a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell, an M3 nut). Leave out sizes, walls, holes and other features (the designer's own spec measures those), a part that must not move at all (a keyed or glued joint, a part that must not spin), bought screws and bolts, and what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

REQUEST
# Bag clip with a living hinge

A clip to close chip bags, in one piece: two arms joined at one end by a thin living hinge, and a
latch at the other end.

- Arms about 100 mm long; the clip closes on a folded bag about 2 mm thick.
- The living hinge is a thin flexible strip that lets the arms fold together; printed open, flat.
- The latch at the free end hooks shut and opens with a thumb.
- PETG on a Bambu Lab A1 with a 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports.

Show me the clip as it prints, open, and it closing as its motion.
